title: AIDA design-closed record
description: What design closed on, at <task folder>/design-closed.json, beside task.json and alignment.json, never inside design/ (ideal/implementation.md, 'Freezing, and what a freeze is for'). It sits at the task's own root because a record inside the folder it hashes would hash itself. Implementation reads this file before it freezes anything and refuses to start when the hash it re-derives from the live alignment.json and design/*.json disagrees with the hash recorded here. Closing again after a further change is the supported way to update it: a later close simply overwrites this file with the new hash. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field alignment.json, every design/*.json, task.json and project.json all carry. A repair reads format-changes.md by this number and applies the change that matches, instead of guessing the old shape from what the file happens to contain. Bumped only when a later change to this schema says so, never for a value change inside an unchanged shape.

pluginVersion.description: The plugin version that wrote this record, copied by design's close from the plugin's own plugin.json. It reads unknown when that file could not be read. A task can span a plugin update, and its records then come from two sets of rules. This field says which version wrote which record (live-run row 134). Nothing reads it back; it is for a person or a later reader.

closedAt.description: The UTC date design closed, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script at the moment of closing, never typed by hand. Closing is not one-shot the way implementation's own snapshot is: a design can be reopened, changed and closed again, and this date is the only trace of when the most recent close happened. It answers how old this close is when implementation refuses against it weeks later.

runMode.description: The run mode the close was made under, passed to design-actions.sh close and never inferred. Implementation reads it to tell an attended close from an unattended one, which is the difference between a design a person saw and one a model closed alone.

closedBy.description: Who was present at the close: person on an interactive close, nobody on an autonomous one. It records who was there, never that they said yes; the per-criterion approval scope records is the only mark of a yes (scripts/alignment-schema.json, author).

hash.description: sha256 over the canonical form of alignment.json and every design/*.json together, in work order id order, computed at closing by scripts/lib/records-hash.sh. Implementation calls the same function against the live files and refuses to start when the two disagree, rather than freezing whatever it finds. This is the field that makes closing load-bearing: a design closed, then edited, then started without closing again is refused instead of silently frozen as if the edit had been what design closed on.

path.description: The process recipe body design read and judged, so a note about it can be traced.

fits.description: Whether that method describes the work this task does, judged once by design's own model after reading the body.

reason.description: One sentence saying why, always, because a verdict without a reason cannot be read later.

recipeFit.description: Design's verdict on the process recipe it followed (ideal/tooling.md), written by `close` from the three --recipe-* flags, absent after --no-recipe, restated by every later close.

files.description: Every <task folder>/design/design-critique-<lens>.md this close carries, sorted, one per finished lens. A critic writes into records/, which the project ignores. The close moves each finished file into design/ before it commits, so one commit carries the record and the evidence it names (live-run row 176). A file without its count line was not finished by its critic, so it stays under records/, is left out and is named on stderr.

findings.description: The sum of those files' `findings: N` last lines, read by `close` from the files and never typed by hand.

outcome.description: How the findings were answered, from `close --critique-outcome`. How many changed an order and how many were left with a reason, in the person's words, one line per flag. `none` when no flag was passed, which is every unattended close (live-run row 135). A count alone said nothing about what changed.

critique.description: What the design critique found before this close, and how it was answered. A person can see later what was read, how much it raised and what came of it. Absent when no critic ran. The findings themselves stay in the files; the critique blocks nothing, and a count here is a pointer, never a verdict.
